system_overview: A refinement-checking module that establishes a formal refinement relationship between the scheduling allocator and the simple allocator. It asserts that every behavior of the scheduling allocator (with its schedule-based allocation policy) is also a valid behavior of the simple allocator (which allocates resources freely). This demonstrates that the scheduling mechanism adds constraints without violating the original specification's properties.
actors_and_components: This module creates an instance of the simple allocator specification within the context of the scheduling allocator. The scheduling allocator's constants (clients and resources) are implicitly passed to the simple allocator instance. The module bridges two levels of abstraction in the allocator design hierarchy.
state_variables: Inherits all state variables from the scheduling allocator: pending requests per client, allocated resources per client, and the client schedule. The simple allocator instance uses only the request and allocation mappings (ignoring the schedule variable).
initial_state: Inherited from the scheduling allocator specification.
actions: Inherited from the scheduling allocator specification. No new actions are introduced.
safety_properties: The module asserts a single theorem: the scheduling allocator specification implies the simple allocator specification. This refinement theorem means that every safety and liveness property satisfied by the simple allocator is also satisfied by the scheduling allocator.
liveness_properties: Liveness properties are inherited through the refinement relationship. The theorem asserts that the scheduling allocator's fairness conditions and scheduling policy together imply the stronger fairness conditions of the original simple allocator.
model_bounds: Uses the same model bounds as the scheduling allocator: 3 clients and 2 resources in the configuration file. The refinement check is done via temporal property verification in the model checker.
additional_assumptions: The module relies on the fact that both specifications share the same constant parameters. The refinement is expressed as logical implication between the two complete temporal specifications. The model checker verifies this implication for the finite instance defined in the configuration.
